findings.title: The 3.2a commit can't pass its own success check
findings.description:
Tasks 3.1 and 3.2 stop rendering `Comprehension:` and `### Adoption Facts`. They only remove the matching unit-test cases in `SectionBuilder.test.ts` and `ContextTemplateEngine.test.ts`. Three end-to-end tests still assert that the removed output appears:
- `packages/core/tests/pipeline-integration.test.ts:184` expects `` `Comprehension: ${COMPREHENSION}` ``. The facts/probe cases at lines 154–175 also assert probe output in the prompt. This block is only deleted in 3.3.
- `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:102` expects `### Adoption Facts` (`FACTS_HEADING`). This file is only deleted in 4.1.
- `packages/mcp-server/tests/integration/adoptionParity.test.ts:116` expects `Comprehension:`. This file is only deleted in 3.6.

So 3.2a's check, "`pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` passes", fails. 3.2a also never runs the MCP tests, so even with that fixed, the commit would land with a failing MCP suite. An agent will either get stuck or pull deletions forward on its own.

Fix: either remove the 3.2a commit and let 3.1–3.2 commit with 3.3–3.6 at 3.7, or move those three deletions into 3.1/3.2 and add `pnpm -r test` to 3.2a's check.

findings.title: Commit steps are checkboxes instead of plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description:
Every commit point is a checkbox, never a plain `**Commit**:` line:
- 2.3 (line 79) is a top-level checkbox task.
- 3.2a (lines 99–101) and 3.7 (131–134) are checkbox tasks.
- 4.1–4.4 have `- [ ] Commit:` sub-items (148, 155, 163, 169).
- 5.1 has one too (186).

This causes two problems under the project rules:
- **Checking off is out of order.** The rules say: implement, run task-checker, then commit, and never make a commit that only checks boxes. A commit checkbox can only be ticked after the commit exists, which forces exactly that box-only commit.
- **The rules see no markers.** They key on `**Commit**:` markers, so this file counts as having none. The default then applies: commit at the end of each top-level task. That conflicts with the placement intended here, such as four separate commits inside section 4 and none in section 1.

Fix: replace each commit checkbox with a plain `**Commit**: <message>` line at the same spot. The placements themselves are good: each one is a compiling, tested point.

findings.title: Nothing proves the fake-`sq` marker would ever fire
findings.description:
5.1's mutation check confirms that the snapshot assertion catches a `.context-forge.toml` write. Nothing confirms that the fake-`sq` marker would catch a spawn. By the time 5.1 runs, 4.4 has deleted the probe, so no code path left in the build can spawn `sq`. If the PATH prepend, the executable bit or the marker path is wrong, "marker does not exist" passes anyway. That assertion is the only automated evidence for the "spawns no `sq`" part of the first functional criterion.

Fix: add one sanity line. In `beforeAll`, run `sq` once through `execFileSync` with the patched `PATH`, assert the marker appears, then delete it before the real runs.

findings.title: The purity test sits after the deletions, not right after the behavior change
findings.description: The brownfield behavior changes in 3.3–3.6. Those tasks delete the old brownfield coverage (`pipeline-integration` brownfield block, `adoptionParity.test.ts`), and its replacement only arrives in 5.1. That leaves the four section-4 commits with no brownfield purity test. This matches the design's step order, and section 4 only removes code that is already dead, so the compiler and the golden test carry it. The cost is the `git show {target}:…` step needed to recover `createBrownfieldCheckout`. Moving 5.1 to just after 3.7 would avoid that step and follow the test-with pattern. This is optional.

findings.title: The purity test's "CLI path" re-creates `build.ts` instead of calling it
findings.description: The CLI runs and the CLI/MCP parity check use "pipeline plus integrator, as `build.ts` does it", not `build.ts` itself. D5 allows this, since all surfaces share `createContextPipeline`. Two things back up the real CLI: 3.5 updates `cli/tests/commands/build.test.ts`, and walkthrough 6.3 steps 1–2 exercise the built CLI. No change needed. Just be aware that parity is checked against a stand-in for the CLI.
